Hey @YassineYousfi, congrats to all the prize winners. Wanted to surface a few things since the prize round seems closed and I didn't see acknowledgement of contributions I think were materially original. Going to focus on the new-approach award since that's the one where I think there's a real case.

The biggest one is the per-pair latent-correction sidecar. Single-dim grid-searched perturbation of HNeRV latents chosen to minimize joint SegNet+PoseNet loss. First shipped in this PR (May 4 09:59 UTC) and [#99](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/99). Not in [#95](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/95) or [#98](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/98) prior. The 2nd-place submission [#103](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/103) is by rem2's own description a "lossless byte-level repack of @BradyMeighan's hnerv_lc_v2 ([#100](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/100)). Decoder weights, latents, and latent-correction sidecar are all his." The 3rd-place submission [#102](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/102) is named hnerv_lc_v2_scale095_rplus1, a re-tune of one constant in this same pipeline. Two of three prize winners stood on this technique and it came from this PR.

On my other PR ([#97](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/97) vibe_coder_final_boss), I also ran a Karpathy-style LLM-driven autoresearch loop, around 195 short-budget proxy experiments where the agent reads the previous result, proposes one algorithmic change, runs the proxy, decides keep or revert. To my knowledge no other submission used this methodology for architecture search, and the resulting mask + dual-head FiLM-conditioned generator was the best mask-based score on the leaderboard by ~0.08 over the next mask-family submission. Documented in §4 of the writeup with the actual experiment ledger.

Per your earlier comment on [#53](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/53) about wanting "credit to be more visible in the leaderboard," this PR's relationship to [#102](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/102) and [#103](https://github.com/commaai/comma_video_compression_challenge/issues/103) doesn't show up anywhere on the public board.

Happy to be told my reading is wrong. To be honest, I've been a comma follower since 2016 and a comma user since 2020, and I've always wanted to contribute or be recognized in some way. This challenge was the first concrete shot at it. I spent weeks on it, literal weeks of compute on my personal 3090 with the autoresearch loop running overnight while I slept, two A100 colab runs, and the night before the deadline I was up till 5am polishing the writeup site while watching Ethan iterate on top of my hnerv_lc_v2 in real time. Just wanted to make sure you saw the new-approach case here in case it's still open.

Sure, updating the table. My reading was that this is mostly built on top of #95 with a perturbation addition. But since many submissions picked up your perturbation trick, you can argue that it's significant enough to be considered novel.
@YassineYousfi appreciate you taking another look, thanks. Learned a ton with this challenge and I can't wait for the next one! Any idea when that'll be?

@BradyMeighan Congratulations on making it onto the leaderboard! I hope you had fun competing in the challenge and learned something new along the way. If you are looking for a job or internship, please email givemeajob@comma.ai with a link to this PR. See you in the next challenge!
